description:
Full epic fixture: parallel and dependent tickets, default ticket review, fix/file/reject as parent judgment, epic close exits goal mode.

## Background

This is the published-cutover proof. Separate from scope-policy (can be a second fixture in this issue or a child comment). Do not combine both policies in one ambiguous test.

## Scenario (ticket policy)

1. Epic with two parallel tickets and one dependent.
2. `/bw run` inject prompt, one open group.
3. Two implementation children on shared branch.
4. Optional: overlap notice + peer message if C is done.
5. Settlement does not close.
6. Review child on one ticket (clean) and one with findings; parent fix/file/reject in scripted turns.
7. Fix assignment + re-review.
8. Dependent unlocks only after parent closed the blocker ticket (bw ready), not because a child settled.
9. Epic close exits run and forgets group.
10. No tmux/landing/registry/worker tools.

## Success criteria

- Fixture logs each step.
- tmux binary not required.
- lint/test/typecheck of the repo under test as implementer/reviewer commands, not a beadwork runner.

## Test plan

- e2e script with great logging (timestamps, issue ids, child ids, packet counts).
- Assert packet coalescing if multiple completions are arranged to be near-simultaneous.

## Considerations

Script the parent model (deterministic fake completions) rather than calling paid LLMs in CI.

comments.text: Published-cutover proof. Script parent turns. Separate ticket-policy fixture; do not mix scope policy into the same ambiguous test.

title: Prove one epic end-to-end with ticket review and no tmux
